statutes.act: It Must Be Shown That The Incriminating Act

facts: On 29.10.2000 at about 12:30 p.m., Kamalabai Atmaram Bohare (PW-1), Kusmanbai Suresh Bohare (PW-2) and Pushpabai Ramesh Bohare (PW-3) were working in their fields situated at village Shivantola.
At that time, Atmaram Bohare and Suresh Bohare (deceased persons) were also present there. Gowardhan (A-1) was also standing on the road side.
Suresh Bohare and Atmaram Bohare after putting paddy at the threshing machine were coming back to their home.
When they reached near the D.P. of electricity situated in the land of Kamalabai, Gowardhan (A-1) passed a comment on them and a quarrel between the parties took place.
Immediately after starting of quarrel, A-2 to A-13 rushed there with weapons and started assaulting Suresh Bohare and Atmaram Bohare.
issues: The admissibility/acceptability or otherwise of the evidence of PWs 1-4 as eye-witnesses
petitioner_arguments: Inasmuch as all the prosecution witnesses, particularly, eye-witnesses PWs. 1-4, who are female members of the family of the complainant and close relatives, the evidence of these related witnesses cannot be relied upon.
The courts below committed an error in convicting the appellants mainly on the ground that the weapons of offence were recovered on their disclosure statements.

With the same allegations and similar circumstances, the women accused persons were acquitted by the trial Court and it is not justified in convicting the male accused based on the very same evidence.
respondent_arguments: There is no bar in accepting the evidence of related witnesses.
Because of their relationship, courts have analysed their evidence carefully and meticulously and ultimately accepted their version.
Recovery of weapons and the medical evidence show that the prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt.
court_reasoning: The evidence of an interested witness does not suffer from any infirmity as such, but the courts require as a rule of prudence, not as a rule of law, that the evidence of such witnesses should be scrutinized with a little care.
Once that approach is made and the court is satisfied that the evidence of the interested witness has a ring of truth such evidence could be relied upon even without corroboration.
